---
title: From Quarto
description: What differs from Quarto, and how to check a project before you move it.
order: 8
---

smalldocs builds the website part of Quarto. A project that uses only that part builds with either
tool, and gives the same pages, the same anchors and the same links. Check a project first:

```bash
smalldocs check docs
```

`check` builds the site into a scratch folder and lists every key it ignores, every broken link, and
every piece of Pandoc's Markdown that it does not read, with the file and the line. It exits with 1
when it finds anything.

## What smalldocs does not do

| Quarto | smalldocs |
|---|---|
| PDF, Word, slides, books, manuscripts | Websites only. A `book` builds as a website |
| Runs `{python}`, `{r}` and `{ojs}` cells | Shows the code and runs nothing. A notebook shows its saved outputs |
| Compiles `.scss` themes | Takes any Bootswatch theme and your CSS. See [Themes](themes.qmd) |
| Lua filters | Runs none. The `linkify.lua` filter is built in |
| Grid tables, citations, cross-references (`@fig-x`) | Not read. Write a pipe table, and a link to the id |
| Every Pandoc extension | CommonMark, tables, footnotes, definition lists, task lists, attributes, fenced divs, callouts, tabsets, maths, raw HTML, shortcodes |
| Algolia search, comments, analytics | A search box over `search.json`; add the rest with `include-in-header` |

## What is the same

- `_quarto.yml`, `_metadata.yml` and front matter, merged in the same order.
- Heading ids, made by Pandoc's rules, so links and anchors written for Quarto keep working.
- Links to `.qmd`, `.md` and `.ipynb` files become links to `.html`; a link that starts with `/` starts at
  the project's root.
- The markup of the page: the same classes and ids, such as `#quarto-sidebar`, `#TOC`, `.callout-note`,
  `.panel-tabset` and `.quarto-grid-item`. CSS written for a Quarto site mostly applies.
- `pre-render` and `post-render`, with the same environment variables.

## Moving a project

1. Run `smalldocs check` and fix what it lists.
2. Run `smalldocs preview`, and look at each page beside the Quarto site.
3. Change the recipe that builds the site from `quarto render` to `smalldocs render`, and
   `quarto publish gh-pages` to `smalldocs publish gh-pages`.
4. If the project has its own `apidocs.py`, consider `smalldocs.api` in its place. See
   [The API reference](api.qmd).
